data.reasoning: Both models agree that the executable and security-critical files (PKGBUILD and openkingdoms.install) are safe and contain no malicious code or injection patterns. The 'inconclusive' verdict from the first model was solely due to API errors when reviewing non-executable metadata files (.SRCINFO and .gitignore), which do not pose an AUR injection risk. The second model successfully reviewed all files and confirmed the package is safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool failure (HTTP 400 API error) in the qwen model when processing .gitignore and .SRCINFO, forcing an 'inconclusive' overall result. The deepseek model successfully processed these files and found them to be standard, benign metadata.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .gitignore and .SRCINFO due to API errors.
learnings: The audit tool's verdict aggregation logic should recognize when 'inconclusive' file verdicts are due to tool errors on non-executable metadata files (like .SRCINFO or .gitignore) and not let them block a 'safe' verdict if all executable files (PKGBUILD, .install) have been verified as safe.
Implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for transient API errors to prevent incomplete audits and unnecessary escalations.
